applied.problem: 'Not the rail's temperature' is too absolute, since a hot rail feels hot; and 'more insulation raises where the copper settles' fails for thin insulation on small wires (critical radius), so it is narrowed to thermal insulation packed round a cable.

A motor's or transistor's losses are not just I²R; '45 °C of headroom' right after 'runs at 55 °C' reads as headroom from 55 °C; and a heavier, thicker cable really does settle cooler (lower resistance), so the mistakes are narrowed.

Screen 9 reads as if 43 A holds 70 °C with the wrap in a 40 °C room; that figure is without the wrap (with it, about 31 A). The 70 °C limit belongs to general-purpose thermoplastic (PVC); 90 °C thermoplastic exists.
